title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is stratifying the Deligne–Mumford ("MD") compactification \hat M_{g,ν} of the moduli stack of genus-g curves with ν marked points. The strata are indexed by MD-graphs G, the stable dual graphs. Each graph has vertices S, edges A (half-edges \tilde A) and legs I. Vertex α carries a genus g_α and ν_α = |\hat I_α| special points (its legs plus its half-edges).

Previous page. He proved codim M_{[G]} = s_1, the number of edges, which is the number of nodes. He called μ(G) = Σ_α (3(g_α−1)+ν_α) = 3(g−1)+ν − s_1 the 'modular dimension' and s_1 the 'modular codimension'.

Top of this page. The open stratum corresponds to the trivial graph: one vertex, no edges, weight g, legs I. It is the simplest stratum. The 'most complex' strata are those of modular dimension 0, i.e. maximal modular codimension 3(g−1)+ν. These are the maximally degenerate curves: every component is a 3-pointed P^1, i.e. pants decompositions, giving 0-dimensional strata.

Compactified stratum. He then defines \hat M_G := Π_{α∈S} \hat M_{g_α, \hat I_α}, where each factor is the DM compactification of M_{g_α, \hat I_α} ≅ M_{g_α, ν_α}. For fixed α, the factor represents the fibred groupoid S ↦ {stable (MD) curves Y_α/S of genus g_α with a monomorphism (\hat I_α)_S ↪ Y_α^{lisse}} (eq. (30)/(31)). The product therefore represents systems (Y_α) of such marked curves (eq. (32), next page).

Next page. He forms Y = ⊔ Y_α and glues along the involution σ on \tilde A to get \hat X = Y/σ. This yields the clutching morphism \hat M_G → \hat M_{g,I}. It is Γ = Aut(G)-equivariant, with Γ acting on \hat M_{g,I} through Γ → S_I. It is a local immersion but not an immersion, since it factors through \hat M_G/Γ.

Aim. All of this is the standard boundary combinatorics of \bar M_{g,n}. It serves the 'structure at infinity' programme: a dévissage of \hat M_{g,ν} into products of smaller moduli stacks, glued along the dual-graph stratification. This feeds the Teichmüller-tower / Galois–Teichmüller ideas of the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical errors. Implicit gaps: (1) the stability condition 2g_α−2+ν_α>0 on each vertex is assumed but not restated; (2) 'local immersion' should be read as unramified/finite onto the closed stratum, with the quotient by Aut(G) giving the normalization of the closed stratum closure. Both are standard and correct.

ideas.what: Codimension of a boundary stratum equals number of edges (nodes); 0-dimensional strata are maximally degenerate curves (all components 3-pointed P^1), codimension 3g−3+ν
ideas.modern_name: dual-graph stratification of \bar M_{g,n}; maximal degenerations / pants decompositions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of modular dimension and 'structure à l'infini'

ideas.what: Compactified stratum \hat M_G = product of \bar M_{g_α, ν_α} over vertices, with modular description as systems of pointed stable curves
ideas.modern_name: \bar M_G = Π_v \bar M_{g(v),n(v)} (graph moduli in Getzler–Kapranov modular operads)

ideas.what: Gluing/clutching morphism \hat M_G → \hat M_{g,I}, Aut(G)-equivariant, unramified, factoring through the quotient by Aut(G)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard dual-graph stratification and clutching maps of \bar M_{g,n}, well documented (Knudsen; later Getzler–Kapranov). The terminology 'modular dimension' already appears in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'avec un poids marqué [?], et bien sûr, un genre donné)' rather than 'cas un poids marqué ≠ [?]'.
'Des strates de ma stratification du graphe associé...' is uncertain. The sense is that the stratum associated with the trivial graph of numerical type (g,ν) is 'la plus simple de toutes!'.
'On étudiera les plus complexes tout' should read 'les plus complexes de toutes' (or similar), which correspond to modular dimension zero, 'ou' (not 'à celui d') maximal modular codimension.
Equation label next to the fibred groupoid is probably (31) rather than (30), since (30) was used on the previous page and (32) follows on the next page.
